metadata.title: EliteFit — Internal Project Plan
metadata.schedule_basis: Seven months including technical integration; website M1–4, integration M5–7, SEO M5–12 after website approval

roles.name: Raoul
roles.responsibility: Sets priorities, agrees what the website must do and makes product decisions.
roles.review: Reviews quality and gathers client approval. Names our internal technical lead.
roles.deliverable: Agreed requirements, priorities and product decisions.

roles.name: Betzy
roles.responsibility: Manages the plan, daily client contact, feedback and open questions.
roles.review: Keeps one current plan and makes sure each decision reaches the right person.
roles.deliverable: One current plan, clear updates and recorded decisions.

roles.name: Ryan
roles.responsibility: Writes the website copy and manages SEO after website approval.
roles.review: Patrick checks facts, Raoul checks quality and the client approval lead approves copy.
roles.deliverable: Approved website copy; SEO plan and pages after approval.

roles.name: Mohammed
roles.responsibility: Designs the website and builds the editable WordPress pages.
roles.review: Works with our technical lead to connect the website and test the full customer journey.
roles.deliverable: Reviewed designs and 12–15 editable WordPress pages.

roles.name: Internal technical lead — to confirm
roles.responsibility: Builds and tests the payment, membership, booking and other agreed system connections.
roles.review: Digital Movement owns this work. Raoul must name the person and confirm their availability.
roles.deliverable: Working, tested system connections and support notes.

roles.name: Patrick
roles.responsibility: Checks offers, membership rules, content facts and staff needs.
roles.review: Tests day-to-day staff use and brings business decisions to the owners.
roles.deliverable: Verified business facts and staff-ready working steps.

roles.name: Putu and Richard
roles.responsibility: Agree business needs, offers and client acceptance.
roles.review: Name one person for routine approvals and identify decisions that need both owners.

tasks.task: Manage team updates, feedback and decisions
tasks.helpers: Raoul; Ryan; Mohammed; Patrick; Putu and Richard
tasks.outcome: One current plan, one feedback list and a clear client approval route.

tasks.task: List and prioritise what the website must do
tasks.outcome: Clear needs for buying passes, joining as a member, editing pages and website quality.
tasks.dependency_note: Initial role and approval setup in P01 allows this work to start. Team coordination continues alongside all seven delivery months.

tasks.task: Agree the core page list
tasks.outcome: An agreed list of 12–15 core pages and clear content needs.

tasks.task: Confirm offers and membership rules
tasks.outcome: Clear pass rules and a decision on fixed-term membership, automatic renewal or both.

tasks.task: Check systems, access and customer records
tasks.outcome: System map, checked access and proposed homes for customer and payment records.
checks: Confirm GymMaster access and enabled features.
Confirm the exact ESB product/account and its purpose.
Check Moka, the F&B tool transcribed as “LaFu”, and the possible all-in-one tool transcribed as “Reserve”. The names and use still need checking.

tasks.task: Check feasible payment, membership and booking routes
tasks.outcome: Feasible routes, known limits and checks needed for the Month 5 connected test.
checks: Check GymMaster’s standard WordPress/member module as the first route to test in Month 5.
Check whether the exact ESB product supports gym passes, memberships and secure on-page checkout, or requires a redirect; prove the chosen route in Month 5.
Confirm card, local-bank and QRIS needs, pass credit towards four-week membership, and fixed-term versus automatic renewal.

tasks.task: Name our internal technical integration lead
tasks.outcome: A named Digital Movement delivery lead with time to build and test the connections.
tasks.dependency_note: Initial role and approval setup in P01 allows this work to start. Team coordination continues alongside all seven delivery months.

tasks.task: Collect website facts, offers and images
tasks.helpers: Patrick supplies and checks facts; Betzy gathers missing items
tasks.outcome: Reliable source material and image permissions, with missing items clearly listed.

tasks.task: Design and review the main page layouts
tasks.helpers: Raoul; Ryan; Patrick; client approval lead
tasks.outcome: Reviewed page designs based on the prototype and agreed customer needs.

tasks.task: Set up WordPress and a private test website
tasks.outcome: Editable pages, private testing and a clear route to release the website.

tasks.task: Run a connected purchase with test data
tasks.outcome: A test purchase creates the correct customer record and confirmation, without a live charge.
checks: Test one complete purchase and the return after payment.
Prove how a successful payment creates or updates the correct member record. No ready-made GymMaster–ESB link has been verified.

tasks.task: Review and approve the connected purchase flow
tasks.outcome: A purchase flow reviewed using a working connected test.

tasks.task: Write, review and approve the website copy
tasks.helpers: Patrick checks facts; Raoul checks quality; client approval lead approves
tasks.outcome: Original copy approved a few pages at a time, so building can continue while Ryan finishes other pages.

tasks.task: Build the agreed editable pages
tasks.outcome: WordPress pages with approved copy, clear navigation and layouts that work on phones and computers.
tasks.dependency_note: P13 is a page-by-page dependency. Start approved templates and pages while the remaining copy is still being written.

tasks.task: Build, check and fix the full system connections
tasks.outcome: Working payment, membership, booking and other agreed connections, with clear support instructions.
checks: Define the source of truth for member, order and payment records.
Confirm whether a CRM and WhatsApp/SMS follow-up are needed; choose the platform, consent rules and opt-out route. GoHighLevel is only a candidate.
tasks.dependency_note: Start connection setup in Month 5. Implement the reviewed purchase flow after P12; complete the build in Month 6 and final checks in Month 7.

tasks.task: Prepare staff for the new integrated journey
tasks.outcome: Staff can handle the new purchase flow, missing confirmations and requests for help.

tasks.task: Test the website and the existing booking/payment route
tasks.helpers: Internal technical lead; Patrick; Raoul; Ryan
tasks.outcome: Website, device and accessibility checks pass. The existing booking/payment route is verified and approved for the Month 4 launch.
tasks.dependency_note: The Month 4 website launch does not claim the new integration is complete. If the existing route cannot be verified, pause launch for a decision.
checks: Check navigation, forms, mobile layouts, accessibility and editable pages.
Verify every website link into the existing booking/payment route and confirm staff support steps.
Do not switch on an untested new checkout. Real payments or bookings need separate explicit approval.

tasks.task: Approve the Month 4 website launch
tasks.helpers: Patrick; client approval lead; Mohammed; internal technical lead
tasks.outcome: Client accepts the website and verified existing booking/payment route; explicit website release Go and recovery owner recorded.

tasks.task: Coordinate the Month 4 website launch and handover
tasks.helpers: Mohammed; internal technical lead; Patrick; Raoul
tasks.outcome: Approved website live and checked. Staff receive editing instructions and support contacts; the verified existing booking/payment route remains available.

tasks.task: Manage SEO from Month 5 through Month 12
tasks.outcome: After website approval, agree and create the first ten SEO pages, then manage the later SEO work through Month 12.
tasks.dependency_note: Starts in Month 5 after Month 4 website approval and launch. It does not wait for the Month 7 integration release. Ryan owns SEO; Mohammed and our technical lead own their support areas.

tasks.task: Prepare staff for the Month 4 website launch
tasks.outcome: Staff can edit pages, explain the existing booking/payment route and find the right support contact.

tasks.task: Test the full new connected journey
tasks.helpers: Internal technical lead; Patrick; Raoul; Ryan
tasks.outcome: Purchase, member records, confirmations and recovery steps pass final tests before release.
checks: Test successful, failed, cancelled and repeated transactions; never grant a pass after a failed payment.
Check duplicate prevention, matching records, consent, approved follow-up and staff recovery steps.
tasks.dependency_note: Technical checks and full-journey tests can overlap in Month 7. Accept each journey only after its required checks pass.

tasks.task: Approve the Month 7 integration release
tasks.helpers: Patrick; client approval lead; Mohammed; internal technical lead
tasks.outcome: Client accepts the new connections; separate explicit release Go, backup and recovery responsibilities recorded.

tasks.task: Release the new connections and complete handover
tasks.helpers: Internal technical lead; Mohammed; Patrick; Raoul
tasks.outcome: Approved connections live and verified. Staff receive final instructions, recovery steps and named support contacts.

approval_rules: Month 4 website launch and Month 7 integration release each need client acceptance and a separate explicit Go.
No real booking or payment without Raoul’s explicit approval.
Sitemap submission requires separate explicit approval.

slides.title: Clear roles. Clear outputs.
slides.subtitle: Digital Movement delivers the website, copy and full technical integration.
slides.note: Ryan is confirmed as copywriter and SEO manager. Mohammed is confirmed as frontend designer and web developer. Betzy is project manager; Raoul is product owner. Our technical integration lead still needs an internal assignment. Patrick reviews daily operations. Putu and Richard still need to name their routine approval contact. After launch, Mohammed supports the website and our technical lead supports the connections. Ryan owns SEO, not technical support.

slides.title: Seven months. Two clear releases.
slides.subtitle: Website live at the end of Month 4. New connections live in Month 7.
slides.note: Timeline aligned to the previous proposal: website Months 1–4, technical backend Months 5–7 and SEO Months 5–12. Early system/access checks in Months 1–2 reduce risk. SEO starts after website approval in Month 5; it does not depend on the Month 7 integration release. Months 8–12 continue SEO beyond the seven-month delivery period. Timeline only is reused from the older proposal; its prices, page counts and coordination-only scope do not apply.

slides.title: Agree the starting point.
slides.subtitle: Clarify the offer, name the technical lead and check access.
slides.note: Confirm the proposed 12–15 core WordPress pages, class/day-pass rules and membership behaviour. Membership may be fixed-term, automatic renewal or both; the client decides. Raoul names our internal technical integration lead. Early checks map accounts and feasibility; the connected test starts in Month 5.

slides.title: Design and build the website.
slides.subtitle: Approve copy in small batches and check system feasibility.
slides.note: Mohammed builds editable templates and approved pages while Ryan writes. Check provider features and access to prepare the later integration. No connected checkout is claimed in Month 2. Review the current booking/payment route for the Month 4 website launch.

slides.title: Complete the website pages.
slides.subtitle: Bring approved copy and editable layouts together.
slides.note: Ryan continues copy review while Mohammed builds approved pages. Prepare the website for Month 4 checks. The new system integration is scheduled for Months 5–7; the website launch uses the existing route only if verified and approved.

slides.title: Approve and launch the website.
slides.subtitle: Launch the website with the verified existing booking/payment route.
slides.note: Test the website, accessibility, forms and existing booking/payment route on phones and computers. If that route cannot be verified, pause launch for a decision. Record client acceptance and explicit Go; prepare backups and a recovery owner. Check the actual public domain, favicon and share image. Sitemap submission needs separate approval. New integration is released in Month 7; SEO starts in Month 5 after website approval.

slides.title: Prove the new connected journey.
slides.subtitle: Run the connected test, start the build and begin SEO.
slides.note: Use test accounts and test data. Prove that a purchase creates the correct record and confirmation before approving the new flow. Real payments and bookings need Raoul’s explicit approval. Connection setup starts now; build the approved flow after review. Ryan starts SEO after website approval, independently of the integration release.

slides.title: Build the connections. Prepare staff.
slides.subtitle: Finish the agreed integration while SEO continues.
slides.note: Our internal technical lead owns full implementation. Mohammed supports the website side. Patrick checks staff steps and support needs. Ryan continues SEO. Keep the approved existing route working until the new flow passes its Month 7 checks.

slides.title: Test, approve and release connections.
slides.subtitle: Finish the seven-month delivery and hand over the new flow.
slides.note: Test successful, failed, cancelled and repeated transactions, matching records, confirmations and recovery steps. Require client acceptance and a separate explicit Go before releasing the new integration. Check the live journey and give staff final instructions and support contacts. SEO continues through Month 12; it does not restart or wait here.

slides.title: We build the connections.
slides.subtitle: Our team owns the implementation and testing. The technical lead is an internal appointment.
slides.note: Delivery timing: early feasibility checks in Months 1–2; connected test and build in Month 5; build in Month 6; connected QA, approval and handover in Month 7. These are dated project findings, not a verified account setup. Public ESB Order QS documentation describes restaurant-style orders and a payment-gateway redirect; it does not confirm gym-pass support, embedded payment or a ready-made GymMaster–ESB link. The exact ESB product/account and purpose must be checked. The October checkout is a demo. An Australian-SMS idea was discussed but has not been configured. Platform subscriptions or provider fees still need to be confirmed; no purchase or payment is authorised by this plan.

slides.title: Ready to shape the backlog.
slides.subtitle: 24 planned work packages. Open a workstream for tasks, owners and results.
slides.note: Prepared for Jira; no project or issues created. Expand a workstream, then a task. All task details appear in the PDF appendix. Dependencies show needed results, not exact dates. P13/P14 use rolling page batches. Website release is P18/P19 in Month 4; new integration release is P23/P24 in Month 7. SEO depends only on the website release.

slides.title: Reliable client care.
slides.subtitle: Our working standard is 100% reliability: own every promise and follow-up.
slides.note: Reliability means keeping commitments and communicating early. An update deadline is not a promise that work will be finished. Betzy owns client follow-up. Check product decisions with Raoul, design/development with Mohammed, and copy/SEO with Ryan. Choose realistic update times with the team. Keep replies warm, brief and concrete; explain what the request means for customers. Never blame a teammate or provider. Only say “fixed” or “checked” after the work and tests are complete.

principles.title: Acknowledge
principles.text: Understand the client’s goal and thank them for feedback.

principles.title: Stay helpful
principles.text: If unsure: “We will look into it.” Check before promising a solution.

principles.title: Set the next update
principles.text: Agree a realistic time. Update before it, even if work continues.

principles.title: Close the loop
principles.text: Explain limits honestly and offer useful alternatives.

voice.reliability: Promise a reliable follow-up. Only promise the solution after the team has checked it.

examples.label: Example client reply
examples.text: “Thanks for your feedback. I’ll check with our team and update you by Thursday, 29 October, 15:00 Bali time (WITA).”

examples.label: Acknowledging feedback — template
examples.text: “Thanks for your feedback. I understand you’d like [goal]. I’ll check [issue] with our team and get back to you by [date, time, time zone].”

examples.label: An uncertain request
examples.text: “We will look into it. I’ll check what’s possible with our team and get back to you by [date, time, time zone].”

examples.label: A delay — send before the agreed time
examples.text: “A quick update: we’re still checking [issue], and I don’t have a confirmed answer yet. I’ll update you again by [date, time, time zone].”

examples.label: If the exact request cannot work
examples.text: “We’ve checked [request]. [Specific constraint] means that approach won’t work. We can offer [alternative] to help you achieve [goal]. I’ll send the details by [date, time, time zone].”

examples.label: Requesting client input
examples.text: “To confirm [decision], could you send [specific item]? Once I have it, I’ll review it with our team. I’ll update you on progress by [date, time, time zone], even if we’re still waiting for the item.”

examples.label: An additional request
examples.text: “Thanks for the suggestion. I’ll check it with Raoul and confirm any effect on the agreed work, timing or cost by [date, time, time zone].”

examples.label: Closing a resolved issue — after testing
examples.text: “We’ve fixed [issue] and checked [relevant customer journey]. You can review it here: [link]. I’ll check in with you by [date, time, time zone] to confirm it works as expected.”
